# Load libraries
pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, tidyverse, lme4,lmerTest,emmeans, performance, broom.mixed, DHARMa)

# Read dataset
df <- read.csv("Data_batches.csv")
# Summary stats for numeric traits by treatment
summary_stats <- df %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    n_fish = n(),
    mean_mass1 = mean(Body_mass1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_mass1   = sd(Body_mass1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_mass2 = mean(body_mass2, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_mass2   = sd(body_mass2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_length = mean(body_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_length   = sd(body_length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(summary_stats)
## # A tibble: 3 × 8
##   treatment n_fish mean_mass1 sd_mass1 mean_mass2 sd_mass2 mean_length sd_length
##   <chr>      <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1 control       51      0.716    0.220      0.674    0.219        3.33     0.333
## 2 high          52      0.696    0.213      0.655    0.204        3.30     0.346
## 3 low           52      0.721    0.196      0.680    0.194        3.36     0.289
# Count of males and females per treatment
sex_counts <- df %>%
  group_by(treatment, sex) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'treatment'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
print(sex_counts)
## # A tibble: 3 × 3
## # Groups:   treatment [3]
##   treatment female  male
##   <chr>      <int> <int>
## 1 control       24    27
## 2 high          23    29
## 3 low           27    25
# Overall descriptive stats for all numeric variables
overall_summary <- df %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mass1 = mean(Body_mass1, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_mass1   = sd(Body_mass1, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_mass2 = mean(body_mass2, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_mass2   = sd(body_mass2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_length = mean(body_length, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_length   = sd(body_length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

print(overall_summary)
##   mean_mass1  sd_mass1 mean_mass2  sd_mass2 mean_length sd_length
## 1  0.7112774 0.2089899  0.6697568 0.2045839    3.330968  0.322234
# Boxplot: Body mass before LPS injection
ggplot(df, aes(x = treatment, y = Body_mass1, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Body mass before LPS injection",
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Body mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Boxplot: Body mass after LPS injection
ggplot(df, aes(x = treatment, y = body_mass2, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Body mass after LPS injection",
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Body mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Boxplot: Body length
ggplot(df, aes(x = treatment, y = body_length, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Body length",
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Body length (cm)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Reshape data into long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Body_mass1, body_mass2),
               names_to = "measurement",
               values_to = "mass")

# Create boxplot
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = treatment, y = mass, fill = measurement)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  labs(title = "Body mass before and after LPS injection",
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Body mass (g)",
       fill = "Measurement") +
  theme_minimal()

# Reshape data into long format
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Body_mass1, body_mass2),
               names_to = "measurement",
               values_to = "mass")

# Boxplot split by sex
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = treatment, y = mass, fill = measurement)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  facet_wrap(~ sex) +
  labs(title = "Body mass before and after LPS injection by sex",
       x = "Treatment",
       y = "Body mass (g)",
       fill = "Measurement") +
  theme_minimal()

# Factor setup (set your preferred reference levels)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control","low","high")),
    sex       = factor(sex),
    tank      = factor(tank),
    fish_id   = factor(fish_id)
  )

# For Type-III tests, use sum-to-zero contrasts
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))
# =========================
# 1) Repeated-measures LMM
# =========================
# Long format (before/after)
df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Body_mass1, body_mass2),
    names_to = "measurement",
    values_to = "mass"
  ) %>%
  mutate(measurement = factor(measurement, levels = c("Body_mass1","body_mass2")))

# Model: mass ~ treatment * measurement * sex + random intercepts for tank and fish
mod_rep <- lmer(mass ~ treatment * measurement * sex + (1|tank) + (1|fish_id),
                data = df_long, REML = TRUE)

# Summary & Type-III ANOVA
summary(mod_rep)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: mass ~ treatment * measurement * sex + (1 | tank) + (1 | fish_id)
##    Data: df_long
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: -644.5
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -2.88376 -0.39374  0.00938  0.39522  2.87371 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name        Variance  Std.Dev.
##  fish_id  (Intercept) 0.0365593 0.19120 
##  tank     (Intercept) 0.0006616 0.02572 
##  Residual             0.0003943 0.01986 
## Number of obs: 310, groups:  fish_id, 155; tank, 24
## 
## Fixed effects:

## treatment2:measurement1      -7.260e-05  1.596e-03  1.490e+02  -0.046    0.964

##             trtmnt2:s1 msr1:1 t1:1:1
## treatment1

anova(mod_rep, type = 3)
## Type III Analysis of Variance Table with Satterthwaite's method
##                             Sum Sq  Mean Sq NumDF   DenDF  F value    Pr(>F)
## treatment                 0.000394 0.000197     2  20.911   0.4990    0.6142
## measurement               0.133234 0.133234     1 149.000 337.8824 < 2.2e-16
## sex                       0.010267 0.010267     1 148.064  26.0373 1.012e-06
## treatment:measurement     0.000011 0.000006     2 149.000   0.0144    0.9857
## treatment:sex             0.000283 0.000142     2 147.835   0.3594    0.6987
## measurement:sex           0.000159 0.000159     1 149.000   0.4041    0.5260
## treatment:measurement:sex 0.000001 0.000000     2 149.000   0.0007    0.9993
##                              
## treatment                    
## measurement               ***
## sex                       ***
## treatment:measurement        
## treatment:sex                
## measurement:sex              
## treatment:measurement:sex    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# R2 (marginal/conditional)
performance::r2(mod_rep)
## # R2 for Mixed Models
## 
##   Conditional R2: 0.991
##      Marginal R2: 0.157
# Post-hoc EMMeans
# a) Treatment differences within each measurement & sex
emm_treat_by_meas_sex <- emmeans(mod_rep, ~ treatment | measurement * sex)
pairs(emm_treat_by_meas_sex, adjust = "tukey")
## measurement = Body_mass1, sex = female:
##  contrast       estimate     SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low   0.00303 0.0559 58.8   0.054  0.9984
##  control - high  0.05962 0.0581 62.7   1.025  0.5638
##  low - high      0.05659 0.0567 57.0   0.998  0.5810
## 
## measurement = body_mass2, sex = female:
##  contrast       estimate     SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low   0.00215 0.0559 58.8   0.039  0.9992
##  control - high  0.05857 0.0581 62.7   1.007  0.5750
##  low - high      0.05641 0.0567 57.0   0.995  0.5830
## 
## measurement = Body_mass1, sex = male:
##  contrast       estimate     SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low  -0.02683 0.0553 58.2  -0.486  0.8784
##  control - high -0.00520 0.0534 51.8  -0.097  0.9948
##  low - high      0.02163 0.0545 54.4   0.397  0.9169
## 
## measurement = body_mass2, sex = male:
##  contrast       estimate     SE   df t.ratio p.value
##  control - low  -0.02730 0.0553 58.2  -0.494  0.8744
##  control - high -0.00597 0.0534 51.8  -0.112  0.9931
##  low - high      0.02133 0.0545 54.4   0.392  0.9190
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates
# b) Before vs After (measurement) within each treatment & sex
emm_meas_by_treat_sex <- emmeans(mod_rep, ~ measurement | treatment * sex)
pairs(emm_meas_by_treat_sex, adjust = "tukey")
## treatment = control, sex = female:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0437 0.00573 149   7.618  <.0001
## 
## treatment = low, sex = female:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0428 0.00540 149   7.919  <.0001
## 
## treatment = high, sex = female:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0426 0.00586 149   7.279  <.0001
## 
## treatment = control, sex = male:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0406 0.00540 149   7.506  <.0001
## 
## treatment = low, sex = male:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0401 0.00562 149   7.139  <.0001
## 
## treatment = high, sex = male:
##  contrast                estimate      SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  Body_mass1 - body_mass2   0.0398 0.00521 149   7.631  <.0001
## 
## Degrees-of-freedom method: kenward-roger
# Simple plot of marginal means (mean ± SE)
emmip(mod_rep, treatment ~ measurement | sex, CIs = TRUE)

# Simulate scaled residuals
res_rep <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = mod_rep, n = 2000)

# 1) Core DHARMa plots (QQ-uniformity, resid vs fitted, etc.)
plot(res_rep)

# 2) Formal tests
testUniformity(res_rep)   # want non-significant

## 
##  Asymptotic one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
## 
## data:  simulationOutput$scaledResiduals
## D = 0.080565, p-value = 0.03576
## alternative hypothesis: two-sided
testDispersion(res_rep)   # mainly for non-Gaussian, but fine to check

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.96672, p-value = 0.803
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_rep)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_rep
## outliers at both margin(s) = 0, observations = 310, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.0009995002
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00000000 0.01182909
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.000999500249875062 ) 
##                                                       0
# 3) Residuals vs key predictors (look for trends / heteroskedasticity)
plotResiduals(res_rep, df_long$treatment,   main = "Residuals vs treatment")

plotResiduals(res_rep, df_long$measurement, main = "Residuals vs measurement")

plotResiduals(res_rep, df_long$sex,         main = "Residuals vs sex")

plotResiduals(res_rep, df_long$body_length, main = "Residuals vs body_length")

# 4) Residual distribution across random-effect levels
boxplot(res_rep$scaledResiduals ~ df_long$tank, las = 2,
        main = "Scaled residuals by tank", ylab = "Scaled residuals")

# ---- Save plots (optional) ----
png("DHARMa_rep_core.png", width = 1200, height = 900, res = 120)
plot(res_rep)
dev.off()
